I turned 21 a little while back, and I was really looking forward to trying out lots of beverages; unfortunately, so far at least, most things taste terrible. I'm still interested, just looking for advice I guess. I've tried a few beers, some whiskey, wine, and rum and coke. That was by far the best. Sorry if this is annoying, I would rather not ask friends.

So I was a heavy drinker through my teens and into my early twenties.

If you don't like it, don't drink. I don't drink anymore purely because I just decided not to.

That being said, liquor isn't going to be very great straight. Try some mixed drinks. Margaritas and pina coladas are a good place to start. Beer is very much an acquired taste. As for wine, don't go straight to a deep red. Try out some of the white wines and "cheaper" wines if you are determined to drink wine.

My recommendation is try new drinks as they come across, but don't try to force yourself to drink anything just to drink.

I guess I was really looking forward to it, and so far things smell so awful I gag. When I tried some different beers, I just wondered why not drink something tasty. Part of me wants to be able to man mode "adult" drinks, but I do feel as if I'm forcing myself a little. Than you for the input.
Just keep trying new things until you find something that spikes your interest. There's millions of drink combinations and different tastes to try.

Yup, a nice and fresh pink wine (rosé wine) is a good start. There are some belgian beers that I like besides my regular IIPA, like boscoli ;)

I'd add a couple of fancy cocktails too: americano (campari, sweet vermouth, soda water and orange slice, on the rocks) blind russian (vodka, coffee liquor and irish cream, on the rocks)
What's your attitude towards liqueurs then? May I suggest Cointreau, Limoncello, Southern Comfort?
I don't really know anything about them, thanks for the tip though.
Do you remember the kind of whiskey (bourbon, scotch, irish?) and was it straight? Also have you tried any hard ciders that's generally my go to not beer.
I think it was straight bourbon whiskey jim bean? Some, maybe all of those words are on the bottle.

If it was Jim Beam try that in coke its pretty solid and a little sweeter than most rum and cokes I've had. Check out http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/photos/classic-cocktails-every-man-should-know.html if you want to try new mixed drinks it'll give you an idea of something you might wanna try.

My personal favorite is New Amsterdam gin & orange juice. You can mix the alcohol to juice ratio pretty high and still have a tasty drink. I think it would be easier to know what you "expected" alcohol to taste like and recommend from there, rather than list an assortment of things you may never heard of before.

As a quick beginner primer, there are SEVERAL types of beers, liquors, and liqueurs available. Taste varies greatly even in the same style of alcohol. A stout beer from company A will taste different from company B, the same with rum, whiskey, and any others you can think of. Also if you're drinking on the cheap, chances are what you buy is going to taste horrible, regardless of what it is.
Beer, more specifically, craft beer, is a very nice drink, with much variety. And it has the added benefit of being healthy. Hops are vegetables, right?
